title: Owning Every Dose: Safety, Scope and the Nervous System
next: Chapter 7, Lesson 2: How drugs get in, move around, and work

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already give ASA, nitro, oral glucose, salbutamol, IM epinephrine and naloxone. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Apply the six rights to every dose, and own the result
  2. Know your bigger BC drug list and what each drug demands
  3. Understand the autonomic nervous system, where most drugs act

Textbook: Chapter 7, PDF pages 433–465
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter 7, pharmacology. As EMRs, you already give medications: ASA for chest pain, nitroglycerin, oral glucose, salbutamol, epinephrine into the muscle, and naloxone. So you know how much a drug can help. Now that you're practising as a PCP, your list gets longer, you get a new route, the IV, and the responsibility for every dose is fully yours. The word pharmacology comes from a Greek word that means both drug and poison, and that is exactly the right attitude. Today we'll cover three things: the six rights of giving medication, your bigger drug list, and the nervous system, where most of your drugs do their work.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第 7 章：药理学。你们作为 EMR 已经在给药了：胸痛给 ASA，还有硝酸甘油、口服葡萄糖、沙丁胺醇、肌注肾上腺素和纳洛酮。所以你们知道一种药能帮多大的忙。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你的药单变长了，多了一条新途径——静脉（IV），而且每一剂药的责任完全在你身上。pharmacology 这个词来自一个希腊词，它同时有「药」和「毒」两个意思，这正是给药时该有的态度。今天讲三件事：给药的六个正确、你变长的药单，以及神经系统——你的大多数药都在那里起作用。

slides.title: The six rights, every dose
slides.body:
1. Patient: confirm identity; check allergies (SAMPLE)
  2. Medication: echo the order, read the label, no abbreviations
  3. Dose: calculate, recheck your math, partner verifies
  4. Route: fits the patient's condition and the speed needed
  5. Time: right frequency; vitals before and after (BC: ASA may go first)
  6. Documentation: drug, dose, route, time, response on the PCR

The wrong drug is the most common medication error.
slides.say: Medication errors are the leading cause of patient safety errors in health care, so every dose goes through the six rights. Right patient: confirm who they are, and check allergies in your SAMPLE history. Right medication: the most common error is the wrong drug, because packages and names can look alike. Say the order back, read the label, and avoid abbreviations. Right dose: many doses depend on weight or age, so do the math, check it, and ask your partner to check it. Then right route, right time, and right documentation. Take vital signs before and after every dose. The one BC exception: ASA may come before vitals. As an EMR you did this for a few simple doses. As a PCP you'll calculate more, so the checks matter more.
slides.sayZh: 在医疗中，给药差错是患者安全差错的首要原因，所以每一剂药都要过「六个正确」。正确的病人：确认身份，并在 SAMPLE 病史里查过敏。正确的药物：最常见的差错就是给错药，因为包装和药名可能很像。要复述医嘱、看清标签、不用缩写。正确的剂量：很多剂量取决于体重或年龄，所以要计算、复核，再请搭档也核一遍。然后是正确的途径、正确的时间和正确的记录。每次给药前后都要测生命体征。BC 唯一的例外：阿司匹林可以在测生命体征之前给。当 EMR 时，你只对几种简单剂量做这些核对；当 PCP 后，你要算的更多，核对也就更重要。

slides.title: You give it, you own it
slides.body:
The person who gives the drug owns the dose

  • Even if your partner drew it up and handed it to you
  • Know each drug's indications, contraindications, side effects
  • Use proper technique to prevent infection and complications
  • Don't trust memory: check your protocol or a drug reference
  • Tell the patient what you're giving; they may refuse
slides.say: Here is a big change from first-responder work. The textbook says that giving medications is one of the main things that separates a paramedic from a first responder. A wrong drug, or the right drug at a wrong dose, can kill. Legally, the person who gives the drug is responsible, even if a partner prepared the syringe and handed it to you. So always know what you are giving and why. For every drug, know the indications, the contraindications, the side effects, and how it works in the body. Under stress, memory fails, so check your protocol or a drug reference when you're unsure. And remember, the patient has the right to refuse, so explain the drug and its likely effects first.
slides.sayZh: 这是和第一反应者工作相比的一大变化。教材说，给药是 paramedic 区别于第一反应者的主要职责之一。给错药，或者药对了但剂量错了，都可能致命。法律上，谁给药谁负责——即使注射器是搭档抽好递给你的。所以永远要清楚自己在给什么药、为什么给。每一种药都要掌握适应症、禁忌症、副作用，以及它在体内怎么起作用。压力之下记忆靠不住，没把握时就查流程或药物参考资料。还要记住，病人有权拒绝，所以先向病人说明这是什么药、可能有什么效果。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: your drug list grows
slides.body:
BC exam drug list: 18 drugs. 11 for all licence levels, 7 for PCPs only.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Chest pain: ASA, nitroglycerin
  • Breathing, anaphylaxis: salbutamol, epinephrine (IM only)
  • Low sugar: oral glucose, glucagon
  • Opioid overdose: naloxone
  • Pain: Entonox, methoxyflurane, acetaminophen, ibuprofen

PCP adds

  • Vascular access (IV): EMRs have none
  • D10W IV for low blood sugar
  • Ipratropium, dexamethasone for bronchospasm
  • Diphenhydramine for allergic reactions
  • Dimenhydrinate, ondansetron for nausea
  • TXA IV for shock from blood loss
slides.say: Here is how your scope changes, using the eighteen drugs on the BC exam list. Eleven are for all licence levels, so you already know them: ASA and nitroglycerin for chest pain, salbutamol and intramuscular epinephrine, oral glucose and glucagon, naloxone, and four pain medications. The right column is new. As a PCP you get vascular access, which EMRs don't have. And you add seven drugs: D10W, which is ten percent dextrose in water, for low blood sugar; ipratropium and dexamethasone for bronchospasm; diphenhydramine for allergic reactions; dimenhydrinate and ondansetron for nausea; and TXA, or tranexamic acid, for shock from bleeding. Each new drug comes with its own doses and contraindications, and they are all yours to know.
slides.sayZh: 用 BC 考纲的 18 种药来看你的执业范围怎么变化。其中 11 种所有执照级别都能用，你已经会了：胸痛用的 ASA 和硝酸甘油，沙丁胺醇和肌注肾上腺素，口服葡萄糖和胰高血糖素，纳洛酮，以及四种止痛药。右栏是新的。作为 PCP，你有了静脉通路，这是 EMR 没有的。你还多了七种药：D10W，也就是 10% 葡萄糖水，用于低血糖；异丙托溴铵和地塞米松，用于支气管痉挛；苯海拉明，用于过敏反应；茶苯海明和昂丹司琼，用于恶心；还有 TXA，即氨甲环酸，用于失血性休克。每种新药都有自己的剂量和禁忌症，这些全都要你自己掌握。

slides.q: You're a PCP. Your partner draws up 50 mg of dimenhydrinate for a nauseated 40 kg patient and hands you the syringe. What do you do?
options: Give it; your partner is responsible for the dose
Give it; 50 mg is the standard adult dose
Stop and recheck: BC dose is 1 mg/kg, so 40 mg, and the dose is yours
Give half now and half in 10 minutes
slides.say: Time for a question. You're a PCP. Your partner draws up fifty milligrams of dimenhydrinate for a nauseated patient who weighs forty kilograms, and hands you the syringe. What do you do? A, give it, because your partner is responsible for the dose. B, give it, because fifty milligrams is the standard adult dose. C, stop and recheck: the BC dose is one milligram per kilogram, so forty milligrams, and the dose is yours. D, give half now and half in ten minutes. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道题。你是 PCP。搭档为一位体重四十公斤、恶心的病人抽了五十毫克茶苯海明，把注射器递给你。你怎么做？A 照给，剂量由搭档负责；B 照给，五十毫克是成人标准剂量；C 停下复核：BC 剂量是每公斤一毫克，应为四十毫克，而且这一剂由你负责；D 现在给一半，十分钟后再给一半。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. In BC, dimenhydrinate is one milligram per kilogram up to a maximum of fifty milligrams, so this patient gets forty. Fifty is only the ceiling, which is why B is wrong. A is wrong because the person who gives the drug is legally responsible, even when someone else prepared it. D is a made-up schedule; you calculate one correct dose and give that.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。BC 的茶苯海明剂量是每公斤一毫克，最大五十毫克，所以这位病人应给四十毫克。五十只是上限，所以 B 错。A 错，因为谁给药谁负责，即使药是别人配的。D 是自己编的给法；应该算出一个正确剂量，然后给这个剂量。

slides.title: Three names for every drug
slides.body:
Chemicalthe molecule's structurelong, rarely used
Genericofficial non-brand namenaloxone
Tradecompany's brand name, ®Narcan
  • Sources: plants, animals, minerals, and the laboratory
  • Check drugs in the CPS or Health Canada's Drug Product Database
  • US apps may use other names (albuterol = salbutamol)
slides.say: Every drug has three names. The chemical name describes the molecule, so it is long and hard to say. The generic name is the official, non-brand name, like naloxone. The trade name, or brand name, belongs to a company, like Narcan, and one drug can have several trade names. The textbook uses generic names, so learn those first. Drugs come from four sources: plants, animals, minerals, and the laboratory. When you need to check a drug, the CPS, the main Canadian drug reference, and Health Canada's Drug Product Database are reliable. Be careful with American apps. They are useful, but some names differ. For example, salbutamol is called albuterol in the United States.
slides.sayZh: 每种药都有三个名字。化学名描述分子结构，所以又长又难念。通用名是官方的非品牌名称，比如 naloxone（纳洛酮）。商品名也叫品牌名，属于某个公司，比如 Narcan，一种药可以有好几个商品名。教材用的是通用名，所以先学通用名。药物有四大来源：植物、动物、矿物和实验室合成。需要查药时，加拿大主要的药物参考书 CPS 和加拿大卫生部的药品数据库（Drug Product Database）都可靠。用美国的 app 要小心，它们好用，但有些药名不同，比如沙丁胺醇在美国叫 albuterol。

slides.title: Canadian drug law in brief
slides.body:
• Food and Drugs Act: safe sale, labels, advertising
  • HPFB (Health Canada) approves and regulates drugs
  • Controlled Drugs and Substances Act: schedules by abuse risk
  • Real content must be 95–105% of the label
  • New drug: about 9 years, animal studies + 4 trial phases
  • Approved drug gets a Notice of Compliance and a DIN
slides.say: Now a quick look at the law. In Canada, the Food and Drugs Act protects the public from unsafe or mislabelled products, and the Health Products and Food Branch, or HPFB, inside Health Canada, approves and regulates drugs. The Controlled Drugs and Substances Act sorts drugs into schedules by their risk of abuse. For example, opioids like morphine are in Schedule One, and benzodiazepines are in Schedule Four. Manufacturing is controlled too: a tablet labelled three hundred milligrams must really contain between two hundred eighty-five and three hundred fifteen. A new drug takes about nine years to reach the market, through animal studies and four phases of human trials. Then it gets a Notice of Compliance and a Drug Identification Number, or DIN.
slides.sayZh: 简单看一下法规。在加拿大，《食品药品法》保护公众免受不安全或标签错误产品的伤害；加拿大卫生部下属的健康产品与食品局（HPFB）负责审批和监管药品。《管制药物和物质法》按滥用风险把药物分成不同附表，比如吗啡等阿片类在附表一，苯二氮卓类在附表四。生产也有管控：标示三百毫克的药片，实际含量必须在二百八十五到三百一十五毫克之间。一种新药大约要九年才能上市，要经过动物实验和四期人体试验。获批后会得到合规通知（Notice of Compliance）和药品识别号（DIN）。

slides.title: Special patients, special doses
slides.body:
PatientWhy it's different
PregnantThe drug affects mother and fetus: weigh benefit vs risk
Infant, childLiver immature until about 6 months; gut absorbs slowly
Older adultSlower liver, gut, kidneys; many drugs; missed or double doses

Pregnancy: check each drug's BC rules (e.g. no ibuprofen or methoxyflurane). If the drug is the only way to save the mother, that comes first.
slides.say: Some patients handle drugs very differently. In pregnancy, every drug affects two patients: it can change the mother's body, and it can directly harm the fetus. So you weigh the benefit to the mother against the risk to the baby. If the drug is the only way to save the mother's life, that comes first. And always check each drug's pregnancy rules; several BC drugs have them, like ibuprofen and methoxyflurane, which are contraindicated. Infants don't reach adult liver function until about six months, and their gut absorbs and clears drugs slowly, so the same dose can act stronger. Older adults are similar: the liver, gut, and kidneys slow down. They often take many drugs that interact, and memory problems can lead to missed doses or accidental overdose.
slides.sayZh: 有些病人对药物的反应很不一样。孕妇用药等于同时影响两个病人：药物可能改变母亲的身体，也可能直接伤害胎儿。所以要权衡母亲的获益和胎儿的风险。如果这种药是救母亲性命的唯一办法，救母亲优先。还要逐个查每种药的妊娠规定——好几种 BC 药物都有，比如布洛芬和甲氧氟烷在妊娠时禁用。婴儿的肝功能大约到六个月才达到成人水平，胃肠吸收和清除药物都慢，所以同样剂量的作用可能更强。老年人类似：肝、胃肠和肾都变慢了。他们常同时吃很多药，彼此相互作用，记忆力下降还可能导致漏服或意外过量。

slides.title: The autonomic nervous system
slides.body:
Most prehospital drugs act through the autonomic (automatic) nervous system.

SympatheticParasympathetic
Modefight or flightrest and digest
Heartfaster, strongerslower, weaker
Airwaysdilateconstrict
Pupilsdilateconstrict
Messengernorepinephrine, epinephrineacetylcholine (ACh)
slides.say: Most drugs you give work through the nervous system, especially the autonomic nervous system, the part that runs automatically, without our control. It has two sides that pull against each other. The sympathetic side is fight or flight. It speeds up and strengthens the heart, opens the airways, and dilates the pupils, and its messengers are norepinephrine and epinephrine. The parasympathetic side is rest and digest. It slows the heart, narrows the airways, and constricts the pupils, and its messenger is acetylcholine. Think of the heart rate as a tug of war between the two sides. A drug that copies the sympathetic side is called sympathomimetic, like the epinephrine you give. A drug that blocks it is called sympatholytic.
slides.sayZh: 你给的大多数药都通过神经系统起作用，尤其是自主神经系统——它自动运行，不受我们意志控制。它有互相拉扯的两边。交感神经负责「战斗或逃跑」：让心跳更快更有力、打开气道、扩大瞳孔，它的化学信使是去甲肾上腺素和肾上腺素。副交感神经负责「休息与消化」：让心跳变慢、气道变窄、瞳孔缩小，它的信使是乙酰胆碱。可以把心率想成两边的拔河比赛。模仿交感作用的药叫拟交感药，比如你给的肾上腺素；阻断交感作用的药叫抗交感药。

slides.title: Receptors: lock and key
slides.body:
A receptor is a lock; the messenger or drug is the key

  • Epinephrine on beta-1 receptors: faster, stronger heart
  • An enzyme, AChE, breaks down ACh to end the signal
  • Nicotinic overload: fast pulse, high BP, twitching, weakness
  • Muscarinic overload: slow pulse, tiny pupils, secretions, wheeze

Organophosphate pesticides disable AChE, so ACh piles up.
slides.say: How does a messenger, or a drug, find its target? Through receptors. Think of a receptor as a lock and the chemical as a key; most locks open only for the right key. Epinephrine fits the beta-1 receptors in the heart, so the heart beats faster and harder. Acetylcholine, or ACh, is cleaned up by an enzyme called acetylcholinesterase, which ends the signal. ACh acts on two kinds of receptors. Nicotinic receptors work at the muscles; overload gives a fast pulse, high blood pressure, twitching, and weakness. Muscarinic receptors are spread through the body; overload gives a slow pulse, pinpoint pupils, and a very wet patient: tears, saliva, secretions, wheezing, vomiting, and diarrhea. Some pesticides cause exactly this by disabling the enzyme.
slides.sayZh: 信使或药物怎么找到目标？靠受体。把受体想成一把锁，化学物质是钥匙；大多数锁只认对的钥匙。肾上腺素正好配心脏的 β1 受体，所以心跳更快更有力。乙酰胆碱（ACh）则由一种叫乙酰胆碱酯酶的酶清除，从而结束信号。ACh 作用于两类受体。烟碱受体在肌肉处起作用，过度刺激会出现脉搏快、血压高、肌肉抽动和无力。毒蕈碱受体遍布全身，过度刺激会出现脉搏慢、瞳孔针尖样缩小，病人「很湿」：流泪、流涎、分泌物多、喘鸣、呕吐、腹泻。有些农药正是通过让这种酶失效造成这些表现。

slides.q: A farm worker sprayed with pesticide has pinpoint pupils, drooling, tearing, wheezing, vomiting, and a pulse of 48. Which receptors are overstimulated?
slides.say: Let's check. A farm worker sprayed with pesticide has pinpoint pupils, drooling, tearing, wheezing, vomiting, and a pulse of forty-eight. Which receptors are overstimulated? A, beta-1. B, muscarinic. C, alpha-1. D, beta-2. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检验一下。一位农场工人被农药喷到，瞳孔针尖样缩小、流涎、流泪、喘鸣、呕吐，脉搏四十八。是哪类受体被过度刺激？A β1；B 毒蕈碱型；C α1；D β2。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, muscarinic. The pesticide disables the enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine, so the parasympathetic side is overloaded: a slow pulse, tiny pupils, and secretions everywhere. Beta-1 stimulation would speed the heart up, not slow it. Alpha-1 tightens blood vessels and raises blood pressure. Beta-2 stimulation opens the airways, the opposite of this wheeze. For BC: the antidotes the book names, atropine and pralidoxime, are not in BC EMR or PCP scope, so you give supportive care and transport.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，毒蕈碱型。农药让分解乙酰胆碱的酶失效，副交感一侧过载：脉搏慢、瞳孔小、到处是分泌物。β1 兴奋会让心跳加快，而不是变慢。α1 让血管收缩、血压升高。β2 兴奋会打开气道，正好和这里的喘鸣相反。BC 提醒：书里提到的解毒药阿托品和解磷定不在 BC EMR/PCP 范围内，所以你做支持治疗并转运。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• More doses by weight: more math, more room for error
  • IV drugs reach the blood at once: no taking them back
  • Interactions: ask about prescriptions, OTC, herbal, street drugs
  • Pregnancy, infants, older adults: think twice about the dose
  • An allergic reaction can follow any drug: reassess every dose
slides.say: So what is new to watch out for? First, many of your new doses are based on weight, like dimenhydrinate at one milligram per kilogram, so there is more math and more room for error. Check it twice. Second, the IV route. When a drug goes into a vein, there is no taking it back, so the six rights matter even more. Third, interactions. Your patient's prescriptions, over-the-counter pills, herbal products, vitamins, and street drugs can all interact with what you give, and they may even be the cause of the call. Fourth, be extra careful with pregnant patients, infants, and older adults. And finally, any drug can cause an allergic reaction, so reassess after every single dose.
slides.sayZh: 那么有哪些新的注意事项？第一，你的很多新剂量按体重算，比如茶苯海明每公斤一毫克，计算多了，出错的机会也多了，要核两遍。第二，静脉途径：药一旦推进静脉就收不回来，所以六个正确更加重要。第三，药物相互作用：病人的处方药、非处方药、草药、维生素和毒品都可能和你给的药相互作用，甚至可能就是这次呼叫的原因。第四，对孕妇、婴儿和老人要格外小心。最后，任何药都可能引起过敏反应，所以每给一剂都要复评。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• BC exam drug list: 18 drugs, 7 of them PCP-only
  • EMRs have no IV; IV access is a PCP skill
  • Epinephrine in BC: IM only
  • Not in BC EMR/PCP scope: opioid painkillers, benzodiazepines, insulin
  • Also not in scope: atropine, pralidoxime (2-PAM), activated charcoal
  • Book examples such as amiodarone are outside the BC list
slides.say: For the BC exam, keep the textbook in perspective. The book is written for all of Canada and mentions many drugs, like amiodarone, morphine, or atropine. Your BC exam list has eighteen drugs, and seven of them are for PCPs only. EMRs have no IV access; that is a PCP skill. Epinephrine in BC is given intramuscularly only. Several drug groups from this chapter are outside BC EMR and PCP scope: opioid painkillers, benzodiazepines, insulin, activated charcoal, atropine, and pralidoxime, also called 2-PAM. You still need to understand them, because your patients take them and the concepts behind them still matter. But on a BC call, don't plan to give them.
slides.sayZh: 备考 BC 时，要摆正教材的位置。这本书面向全加拿大，提到很多药，比如胺碘酮、吗啡、阿托品。你的 BC 考纲药单是 18 种，其中 7 种只有 PCP 能用。EMR 没有静脉通路，那是 PCP 的技能。BC 的肾上腺素只用肌注。本章里有几类药不在 BC EMR/PCP 范围内：阿片类镇痛药、苯二氮卓类、胰岛素、活性炭、阿托品和解磷定（2-PAM）。你仍然要理解它们，因为病人会用这些药，背后的原理也仍然重要。但在 BC 出车时，不要打算给这些药。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Six rights on every dose; whoever gives it owns it
  2. PCP adds IV access and 7 drugs, each with its own limits
  3. Sympathetic: fight or flight; parasympathetic: rest and digest

Next: how drugs get in, move around, and work
slides.say: Let's wrap up. One: use the six rights on every dose, and remember that the person who gives the drug owns it, even if a partner prepared it. Two: as a PCP you add IV access and seven new drugs: D10W, ipratropium, dexamethasone, diphenhydramine, dimenhydrinate, ondansetron, and TXA. Each one comes with its own dose and contraindications. Three: the autonomic nervous system has two sides, fight or flight and rest and digest, and drugs act on them through receptors, like keys in locks. Next lesson, we'll follow a drug from the moment you give it: how fast each route works, what the body does to the drug, and what the drug does to the body. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，每一剂药都要过六个正确；谁给药谁负责，哪怕药是搭档配的。二，作为 PCP 你多了静脉通路和七种新药：D10W、异丙托溴铵、地塞米松、苯海拉明、茶苯海明、昂丹司琼和 TXA，每种都有自己的剂量和禁忌症。三，自主神经系统有两边——「战斗或逃跑」和「休息与消化」，药物通过受体作用于它们，就像钥匙开锁。下节课我们从给药那一刻开始跟踪一种药：各途径起效多快、身体怎么处理药物、药物又怎么作用于身体。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
